figures.title: Figure 3
figures.summary: AM 1.5 device I–V response with four treatment-time rows. All photovoltaic values describe complete QDSC devices, not intrinsic Cu2S properties.
figures.scope_label: Figure inset explicitly reports the 2, 5, 8 and 12 h treatment-time variants; device batch IDs/replicates are not given.

figures.title: Figure 1
figures.summary: Powder XRD trace and reference reflections; paper reports hexagonal chalcocite indexing and an approximately 25 nm Scherrer coherent-domain estimate.
figures.scope_label: 5 h autoclave powder for XRD; exact batch/specimen link to graphite SEM and QDSC measurements is not reported.

figures.title: Figure 2
figures.summary: Graphite paper before treatment (a) and after the 5 h Cu2S treatment (b). The article describes spread-dispersed particles; no numeric particle-size distribution is reported.
figures.scope_label: Panel a is untreated graphite; panel b is treated graphite after 5 h. Working distance is panel-specific: 5.7 mm for a and 5.8 mm for b.

figures.title: Figure 4
figures.summary: Device-level comparison includes the Nano-Cu2S/C route and literature/control counter electrodes; other electrode curves are not separate Deng synthesis routes.
figures.scope_label: Only the Cu2S/C comparator is linked to the 5 h source route; control/device construction is comparison context.

figures.title: Figure 5
figures.summary: Nyquist plots and equivalent circuit. Authors assign the high-frequency semicircle to counter-electrode/electrolyte charge transfer; reported Cu2S/C Rct is 0.063 Ω cm².
figures.scope_label: Whole-device/electrode-interface context; exact physical sample/batch linkage to Fig. 3 is not supplied.

intuition.title: Author motivation
intuition.summary: The article frames the work as a low-cost flexible Cu2S/carbon counter-electrode route for QDSCs, using flexible graphite paper as the conducting support.

source_locator.locator: Main PDF p. 2, printed p. 987, Experimental, Preparation of Counter Electrode

intuition.title: Author interpretation
intuition.summary: The authors propose that air annealing can add surface functionality that helps the Cu2S layer adhere, and discuss dispersed deposits and lower interface resistance as useful for cell operation. These are attributed interpretations, not separately measured causal mechanisms.

general_background.title: Solvent and a closed reaction environment
general_background.summary: A heated closed solvent environment changes solubility, transport and precursor conversion compared with an open vessel. Changes in solvent properties and dissolution followed by reprecipitation can alter the pathways available for nucleation and crystal growth.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Mechanisms of Nucleation and Growth of Nanoparticles in Solution

general_background.title: Conversion of a nonmetal precursor
general_background.summary: Chalcogen and pnictogen precursors can differ in how they release or transfer the element during a reaction. Bonding, coordination and the reaction medium can influence the activation or transfer steps that make an element available for growth.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
